---
title: "CLT Convergence for Binomial Distribution"
format: html
editor: visual
---

## Background

A binomial distribution is the number of successes given p = the chance of success and size = the number of tries to get a success. Given p = 0.10, this is going to look similar to an exponential function, and therefore is likely to take a while to converge.

## Data

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# Monte Carlo Simulation: Binomial Small Parent (size = 5, p = 0.10)
# ==============================================================================

library(ggplot2)

# 1. Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(6418)

# 2. Simulation parameters
B <- 10000                            # Number of Monte Carlo repetitions
n_values <- c(2, 5, 10, 30, 100)      # Sample sizes to test
size_param <- 5                       # Trial size (n_0)
prob_param <- 0.10                    # Success probability (p)

# 3. Initialize storage
results <- data.frame()
sim_data <- list()                    # List to store raw sample means vectors

# 4. Run Monte Carlo loop for Binomial Small
for (n in n_values) {
  
  # Draw B sample means from Binomial(size = 5, prob = 0.10)
  sample_means <- replicate(B, mean(rbinom(n, size = size_param, prob = prob_param)))
  
  # Save raw sample means for visual validation graphs
  sim_data[[as.character(n)]] <- sample_means
  
  # A. Calculate Q-Q Plot R-squared
  theo_quantiles <- qnorm(ppoints(B))
  sample_quantiles <- sort(sample_means)
  r2_val <- cor(theo_quantiles, sample_quantiles)^2
  
  # B. Calculate Sample Absolute Skewness (3rd standardized moment)
  m3 <- mean((sample_means - mean(sample_means))^3)
  s3 <- sd(sample_means)^3
  skew_val <- abs(m3 / s3)
  
  # C. Calculate Sample Absolute Excess Kurtosis (4th standardized moment - 3)
  m4 <- mean((sample_means - mean(sample_means))^4)
  s4 <- sd(sample_means)^4
  kurt_val <- abs((m4 / s4) - 3)
  
  # Append to results data frame
  results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
    n = n,
    R2 = r2_val,
    Skewness = skew_val,
    Excess_Kurtosis = kurt_val
  ))
}

# Print numerical summary table to console
print(results)

# ==============================================================================
# Generate Diagnostic Plots with 3xSE Threshold Overlays
# ==============================================================================

# Graph 1: Q-Q Plot R^2 vs. Sample Size (Threshold = 0.98)
p1 <- ggplot(results, aes(x = n, y = R2)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.98, linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = max(n_values), y = 0.98, label = "Threshold (0.98)", 
           vjust = -0.5, hjust = 1, color = "firebrick", fontface = "bold") +
  labs(
    title = expression(bold("1. Quantile Alignment (" * R^2 * " vs. Sample Size)")),
    subtitle = "Binomial Small Parent (size = 5, p = 0.10)",
    x = "Sample Size (n)",
    y = expression("Q-Q Plot " * R^2)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = n_values) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.95, 1.001)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# Graph 2: Absolute Skewness vs. Sample Size (Threshold = 0.075)
p2 <- ggplot(results, aes(x = n, y = Skewness)) +
  geom_line(color = "darkorange", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "darkorange", size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.075, linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = max(n_values), y = 0.075, label = "Threshold (0.075)", 
           vjust = -0.5, hjust = 1, color = "firebrick", fontface = "bold") +
  labs(
    title = "2. Asymmetry (|Skewness| vs. Sample Size)",
    subtitle = "Binomial Small Parent (size = 5, p = 0.10)",
    x = "Sample Size (n)",
    y = "|Skewness|"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = n_values) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.3)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# Graph 3: Absolute Excess Kurtosis vs. Sample Size (Threshold = 0.15)
p3 <- ggplot(results, aes(x = n, y = Excess_Kurtosis)) +
  geom_line(color = "forestgreen", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "forestgreen", size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.15, linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = max(n_values), y = 0.15, label = "Threshold (0.15)", 
           vjust = -0.5, hjust = 1, color = "firebrick", fontface = "bold") +
  labs(
    title = "3. Tail Weight (|Excess Kurtosis| vs. Sample Size)",
    subtitle = "Binomial Small Parent (size = 5, p = 0.10)",
    x = "Sample Size (n)",
    y = "|Excess Kurtosis|"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = n_values) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.5)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# Display diagnostic plots
print(p1)
print(p2)
print(p3)
```

R\^2 passes between 10 and 30, kurtosis passes between 2 and 5, but skewness doesn't pass even at n=100. Let's look at skewness for even larger values of n.

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# Refinement Simulation: Binomial Small Parent (Skewness Crossover - Coarse)
# ==============================================================================

# 1. Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(6418)

# 2. Simulation parameters
B <- 10000                            # Number of Monte Carlo repetitions
n_values <- seq(100, 1000, by = 100)  # Multiples of 100 between 100 and 1000
size_param <- 5                       # Trial size (n_0)
prob_param <- 0.10                    # Success probability (p)

# 3. Initialize storage
results <- data.frame()
sim_data <- list()                    # List to store raw sample means vectors

# 4. Run Monte Carlo loop for Binomial Small
for (n in n_values) {
  
  # Draw B sample means from Binomial(size = 5, prob = 0.10)
  sample_means <- replicate(B, mean(rbinom(n, size = size_param, prob = prob_param)))
  
  # Save raw sample means to sim_data
  sim_data[[as.character(n)]] <- sample_means
  
  # Calculate Sample Absolute Skewness
  m3 <- mean((sample_means - mean(sample_means))^3)
  s3 <- sd(sample_means)^3
  skew_val <- abs(m3 / s3)
  
  # Append to results data frame
  results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
    n = n,
    Skewness = skew_val
  ))
}

# ==============================================================================
# Generate Skewness Plot with 0.075 Threshold Overlay
# ==============================================================================

p_skewness_zoom <- ggplot(results, aes(x = n, y = Skewness)) +
  geom_line(color = "darkorange", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "darkorange", size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.075, linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = max(n_values), y = 0.075, label = "Threshold (0.075)", 
           vjust = -0.5, hjust = 1, color = "firebrick", fontface = "bold") +
  labs(
    title = "Asymmetry (|Skewness| vs. Sample Size)",
    subtitle = "Binomial Small Parent (size = 5, p = 0.10) — Coarse Search",
    x = "Sample Size (n)",
    y = "|Skewness|"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = n_values) +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# Display plot
print(p_skewness_zoom)
```

There's a lot of noise as a result of the monte carlo simulations, though a downward trend is still apparent. It doesn't make sense to try and come up with a specific number given the size of the error, so instead I will say that n is somewhere between 200 and 1000.

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# Visual Validation Plots for Binomial Small Parent at n = 1000
# ==============================================================================

# Extract raw n = 1000 sample means from sim_data list
df_n1000 <- data.frame(sample_means = sim_data[["1000"]])

# Graph v1: Histogram + Density (Unimodality Check)
v1 <- ggplot(df_n1000, aes(x = sample_means)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)), 
    bins = 50, 
    fill = "steelblue", 
    color = "white", 
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_density(color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(
    title = expression(bold("Visual Check for Unimodality")),
    subtitle = "Sample Means at n = 1000",
    x = "Sample Mean",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# Graph v2: Normal Q-Q Plot for n = 1000
v2 <- ggplot(df_n1000, aes(sample = sample_means)) +
  stat_qq(color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  stat_qq_line(color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = expression(bold("Normal Q-Q Plot")),
    subtitle = "Sample Means at n = 1000",
    x = "Theoretical Quantiles",
    y = "Sample Quantiles"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# Display visual validation plots
print(v1)
print(v2)
```

## Conclusion

As expected, the n value for convergance to normality is quite high. Even at n=1000, visual inspection shows odd pretty clear changes from expected. This cannot be a result of the discreteness of the function, since the value of n is high enough that the means can occur every multiple 0.001.

## $$\boxed{n=\text{200 to 1000}}$$
